page.layout: One column of running text, set in roman and italic type. Running head at the top with the page number at its left. No marginal notes. Catchword at the lower right.

main_text.p: Controv. Lib. i. C. v. Quanquam hic invi-diosius Luthero circa Libros Iobi & Ec-clesiastis, imò optimis Albigensibus sce-leratæ cum Antinomis conspirationis at-que consensus noram[?] inusserit.

II. Vix tamen usque adeo disceptatum ac de authoritate nobilissimæ illius Epistolæ quæ inscribitur ad Hebræos. Scilicet ab iis constantissimè damnata, quorum semper dogmatibus adversa fuit. Repudiavit Marcion, cum primis ex odio Ve-to Testamenti, indignatus typos cum antitypis, umbras cum corpore, figuras cum expressiori rerum imagine, vaticinia cum complemento, Vetus Testamentum cum Novo, quàm accuratissimè hanc in Epistolâ conferri. Eadem fuit iniquitate Ebion, Legis & ceremoniarum præpo-stero quàm zelo. Eadem Arrius, Antitrinitarii alii, ob assertam in eâ luculenter ac vindicatam Divinitatem filii Dei, illius τὸ ὁμοούσιον καὶ συναΐδιον. Accesserè Latini nonnulli Veteres, cum Afri, tum imprimis Romani, ad Hieronymi fere usque tempora, maximè quia Novato & Nova-

page.notes: Doubtful readings: "noram" (probably a printed form of "notam"); the Greek phrase after "illius" is partly unclear, in particular the conjunction; "Ve-to" at the line end (probably a printed form of "Veteris"); the phrase "cumprimis" is printed as one word. Long s has been set as plain s throughout. The catchword "Nova-" is at the lower right, and the text ends with "Novato &" above it.
